clue.text: A man for all seasons?

blocks.note: surface reading: the title of the play about Thomas More, a man of steady principle
setter's reading: seasons is a verb, flavouring food, so the man is one who adds flavour to everything

explanation.surface: A nod to Robert Bolt's play about Sir Thomas More.
explanation.walkthrough: A SPICER is one who spices, and spicing food is seasoning it; the question mark flags the play on words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who adds pepper, cloves and other flavourings to dishes is literally a seasoner of them.

clue.text: Outlaw professional writing

blocks.note: a pro is a professional
script is handwriting or written text

explanation.surface: A criminal who writes for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: A proscript is an archaic term for a person who has been proscribed, banished or declared outside the protection of law.

clue.text: Fruit - a hag almost swallows it

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word for a hag is dropped
to swallow is to take something inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: a crone is a hag; almost all of it is kept
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old witch gobbling a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The citron is a large lemon-like citrus fruit whose thick peel is often candied.

clue.text: Traveller goes over the brink and gets the rap

blocks.note: a rep, or commercial traveller, is a travelling sales representative
a brink is an edge or rim
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller oversteps the mark and is punished for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rap, as in a rap on the knuckles, is a sharp rebuke or telling-off.

clue.text: Fascination of ecclesiastical body with weaponry

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
arms are weapons

explanation.surface: The allure of an armed church.
explanation.definitionFit: Charms are attractive qualities that fascinate or captivate other people.

clue.text: Albert, writer of "Tree Climbing"

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word is read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: the sumac is a shrub or small tree

explanation.surface: An imaginary title by a famous author about scaling trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make "Tree Climbing" look like a book title, but it is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Camus was the French writer of The Outsider and The Plague.

clue.text: A girl gets old without the means

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following article is taken away from the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written
Vera is a girl's name
to age is to grow old
an article, swapped for its indefinite form a

explanation.surface: A young woman grows old in poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without the means' reads as being poor, but 'without the' tells you to drop an article, A, from the word for gets old.
explanation.definitionFit: Averages are arithmetic means, the sum of values divided by their count.

clue.text: Saul's clan involved in numerous matrimonial disputes

indicators.note: something involved in a phrase is wrapped up inside its letters

blocks.note: found running through these words

explanation.surface: A family caught up in many marital quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible (1 Samuel 10:21) Saul was chosen from the family of the Matrites, the clan of MATRI; 'numerous' and 'disputes' are surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament, King Saul came from the Benjamite family descended from Matri.

clue.text: Put duck back in pot, for it's on the house

indicators.note: to put one thing in another is to place it inside
back tells us to read the combined letters from right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction to return the duck to the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: The duck goes into 'pot, for' between the O and R, and the whole string is then read backwards; 'for' looks like a link word but is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooftop is the top of a building, quite literally sitting on the house; 'on the house' also hints at something free.

clue.text: Constable's qualification, for example, is helpful to drivers

blocks.note: surface reading: a police officer's or painter's credentials, given as an example
setter's reading: RA, as the painter Constable was a Royal Academician, and EG for 'for example'; turned round, these letters spell a word for a car's cogs

explanation.surface: A constable's qualifications help motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: RA and EG read backwards give GEAR, so the instruction 'reverse' plus GEAR describes the wordplay; REVERSE GEAR is also what drivers use to back up.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverse gear is the setting in a car's gearbox that lets motorists drive backwards.

clue.text: West gets around in Wales

indicators.note: turning around means the following word is read back to front

blocks.note: Mae West was the Hollywood film star
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller heading west wanders about in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like a compass point, but it is the actress Mae West.
explanation.definitionFit: Maesteg is a town in the Llynfi valley of Bridgend county in South Wales.

clue.text: Common stainer - with Punjabi blood?

definitions.note: a figure with blood on his hands in the Punjab

blocks.note: general means common or widespread
a dyer stains cloth with colour

explanation.surface: An ordinary dyer with Indian ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punjabi blood' sounds like ancestry, but means blood spilled in the Punjab.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer ordered the 1919 Amritsar massacre in the Punjab, killing hundreds of unarmed people.

clue.text: "The Queen!" - toast in fashion in Belgravia

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so these letters are worked into a new form

blocks.note: Queen Victoria
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A royal toast drunk among the smart set of Belgravia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fashion' reads as stylish, but 'in' belongs to the letters being rearranged. Belgravia is a wealthy district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria Station, the London rail terminus, sits on the edge of the Belgravia district.

clue.text: Scoff, perhaps, at 11

blocks.note: first meaning: to scoff at or berate them
second meaning: what you find at the London terminus answering 11

explanation.surface: Eating, or mocking, at eleven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' suggests eating in British slang, but here it means jeer; 11 points to the station answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to complain bitterly or abuse, and trains run on rails at a station.

clue.text: Paperback about awful stench near Salford

indicators.note: about means placed around the outside of what follows
something awful is in a bad state, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets; here it comes back to front
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheap book about an unpleasant smell in the north-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paperback' reads as a cheap book, but splits into paper, a ream, and back, meaning written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchester is the large city right beside Salford, separated only by the River Irwell.

clue.text: What the doctor ordered after Tom became morbidly inflexible

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat
a tonic, as in 'just what the doctor ordered'

explanation.surface: A patient named Tom grew stiff after taking his prescription.
explanation.walkthrough: The block reading 'what the doctor ordered' comes after Tom in the answer, as 'after' says.
explanation.definitionFit: A catatonic person is in a stupor with rigid, immobile muscles, a medical condition of abnormal rigidity.

clue.text: Schemer's play opening in strange antic

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the other
strange means odd or altered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: these letters rearranged
Act I is the opening of a play

explanation.surface: A schemer's drama begins with a bizarre caper.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactician is someone skilled at planning manoeuvres and plotting moves to gain advantage.

clue.text: They may investigate race matters

blocks.note: surface reading: officials looking into questions of ethnicity and racial issues
setter's reading: the officials at a horse race who look into disputes and infringements

explanation.surface: An inquiry into racial issues.
explanation.walkthrough: At British race meetings, stewards hold inquiries into objections and possible rule breaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing stewards are the officials who adjudicate disputes and enforce rules at horse races.

clue.text: Unpopular beat for coppers?

blocks.note: surface reading: a police patrol on a housing estate that officers dislike
setter's reading: a hated tax, levied on a dead person's property

explanation.surface: Police officers dread patrolling a rough housing estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Coppers are police officers, and a beat is a patrol round; an estate here is both a housing estate and a dead person's property, with coppers also hinting at money.
explanation.definitionFit: Estate duty was the British tax on inherited property, long resented as death duty.

clue.text: Coca Cola's method of seeking a contract?

indicators.note: the possessive says the letters belong to, and sit inside, the brand name before it

blocks.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: A soft-drinks firm's approach to winning a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: ACOL is the bidding system most used in British bridge, where a contract is the number of tricks a side undertakes to win.
explanation.definitionFit: Acol is a bridge bidding system, the way partners negotiate towards the contract they will play.

clue.text: Hood left over the door

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship
a hood is a hoodlum, such as the gangster Al Capone

explanation.surface: A cowl left hanging above a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'over' puts the word for left above the gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: A portal is a doorway or grand entrance, especially an imposing one.

clue.text: Women tend to be erratic with course of action for long-term provision

indicators.note: being erratic means behaving unpredictably, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: these letters rearranged
a policy is a planned course of action

explanation.surface: Women being unpredictable about planning for the future.
explanation.definitionFit: An endowment policy is a life insurance savings plan that pays out after a fixed long term.

clue.text: It's almost modest to hesitate

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the last letter of the word for modest is lost

blocks.note: demure means modest; almost all of it is kept

explanation.surface: Shyness is close to reluctance.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection or show reluctance before agreeing.

clue.text: The old soldiers held up their adversary

indicators.note: something held is gripped inside, so the soldiers sit within the old word
in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: ye is an old form of the
soldiers are men

explanation.surface: Veteran troops were ambushed by their foe.
explanation.definitionFit: An enemy is an opponent or foe, someone hostile to you.

clue.text: Regret over Rome's destruction

indicators.note: destruction breaks something apart, so the letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Sorrow at the sack of the Eternal City.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret or guilt felt for a wrong one has done.

clue.text: A painter is comparatively smart  ...

blocks.note: first meaning: Jean-Marc ..., the French portrait painter
second meaning: the comparative of natty, meaning smart

explanation.surface: One artist is more stylish than others.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means neat and smartly dressed, and Nattier was an eighteenth-century court portraitist.

clue.text: ...  but his rejected output shrinking and worthless

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a painter's output is his art
shrinking means timid or shy

explanation.surface: The painter's discarded canvases are dwindling and of no value.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the painter in the previous clue, so 'his output' is a painter's art.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashy describes something cheap, of poor quality and of little value.

clue.text: Officer on unknown outpost

blocks.note: Col is short for colonel
taken as written
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: An officer posted to a remote, unnamed station.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony is a settlement in a distant territory controlled by a far-off power.
